alignments.note: Finite verb recast as 'They shall have ... to eat', discontinuous around the object (rule 25). Dropping 'have' leaves the clause with no finite verb, so the word completes this verb's rendering rather than being an added possession (rule 43).
The single English 'portions' assigned to the first חֵלֶק, which is the clause's object and the English noun's role; the competing reading gives it to the second, standing after 'like'.
לְבַד fused to 'besides' (rule 30), headed on the noun carrying the lexeme (rule 23).

The noun is recast as a relative expression, 'that which cometh of the sale'; the supplied antecedent, relative and verb join its unit and none is added (rule 46's closing rider). Head on the word carrying the lexeme.
Suffix as possessive, relocated by the ASV onto 'patrimony' (rule 18).
The phrase's one determiner is the possessive answering to the suffix, so no 'the' answers to this article (rule 41's limit).

review_notes: 'shall have ... to eat' kept whole with יֹאכֵלוּ, since the subtraction test leaves the verb with no finite predicate if 'have' is removed.
Which חֵלֶק carries the single 'portions' is a genuine tie; the choice and the alternative are recorded in that unit's note.
